races.title: State Assembly, District 30
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Shannon Kessler
cands.bio: Republican candidate for California Assembly District 30 in 2026. Real estate broker and co-owner of a family construction company and real estate business on the Central Coast. Former Arroyo Grande Parks and Recreation Commissioner and PTA president. Founded Save Girls' Sports Central Coast.

endorsements.text: Endorsed by the Republican Party of California, Reform California, and voter guides including April's Common Sense Cali Voters and The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn (per Ballotpedia).

Her Ballotpedia survey also lists the American Independent Party of California, the San Luis Obispo, Monterey, Santa Cruz and Santa Barbara County Republican Parties, Sonja Shaw (candidate for State Superintendent of Public Instruction), and Lucia Mar school trustees Mike Fuller and Eilene Pham.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Shannon Kessler was born or raised, or when she came to California. She says she is from a sixth-generation California family and has raised her family on the Central Coast. We found no record of her specific actions or decisions as an Arroyo Grande Parks and Recreation Commissioner. We found no documented positions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B visas or immigration enforcement, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. Her stated positions on development, public safety and education are general. No controversies, foreign ties or news coverage beyond her campaign materials and Ballotpedia turned up.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: She is a real estate broker and co-owner of a local family construction company and real estate business. She also served as an Arroyo Grande Parks and Recreation Commissioner and as a PTA president. She has held no legislative office.
qual.why: Business ownership and real estate work put her in the middle band. The parks commission, PTA and advocacy groups add nothing under the rubric, and she has no legislative, law, policy or budget career.
qual.label: Business ownership and real estate work put her in the middle band. The parks commission, PTA and advocacy groups add nothing under the rubric, and she has no legislative, law, policy or budget career.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Says she supports responsible environmental protection, including limits on offshore drilling, and 'thoughtful land stewardship' to protect the Central Coast's coastline, agriculture and natural beauty. She gives no specific position on growth limits or rezonings.

back-police-order.evidence: Says she wants public safety policies that 'hold offenders accountable' and addresses retail theft and repeat crime. She gives no specific position on police pay, pensions or penalties.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Dawn Addis
cands.bio: Democratic member of the California State Assembly for District 30 since December 2022. Former special education teacher in San Luis Coastal Unified School District for about 20 years. Served on the Morro Bay City Council from 2019 to 2022. Co-founded the San Luis Obispo Women's March. Chairs the Assembly Budget Subcommittee on Health.

endorsements.text: Endorsed in 2026 by the Democratic Party of California, the California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), the California Nurses Association, SEIU Local 521, IUOE Local 3 and the National Union of Healthcare Workers.
Endorsed in 2026 by California Environmental Voters and Equality California.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Dawn Addis was raised or when she moved to the Central Coast. We also could not find the year she began teaching. We found no documented statements or actions by her on data centers, a homestead property tax exemption, limits on investor or foreign land buyers, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, or school vouchers and charters. Her statements about housing in her candidate survey mix support for cutting red tape with support for smart growth, so we did not classify them. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 40: Ballotpedia lists her birthplace as San Francisco and she earned both degrees at San Francisco State University. Wikipedia reports about 20 years teaching in San Luis Obispo, and she served on the Morro Bay council from 2019, but her upbringing and the dates she started living on the Central Coast are not given.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2022, including a term as Assistant Majority Leader for Policy and Research, and a member of the Budget Committee. Morro Bay city councilmember and mayor pro tem 2019-2022. Worked about 20 years as a special education teacher and program developer.
qual.why: She has prior legislative service, chamber leadership as Assistant Majority Leader, and local elected office, plus budget-committee work and a long education career. Her chairing of a budget subcommittee is not counted.
qual.label: She has prior legislative service, chamber leadership as Assistant Majority Leader, and local elected office, plus budget-committee work and a long education career. Her chairing of a budget subcommittee is not counted.

pro-life.evidence: Planned Parenthood of California gave her a perfect voting-record score, as reported by Wikipedia, and she has served on the board of the Planned Parenthood Central Coast Action Fund. These are reports of her record, not individual roll calls.

second-amendment.evidence: The NRA Political Victory Fund gave her an F rating and Moms Demand Action named her a 2026 Gun Sense Candidate, as reported by Wikipedia. These are group ratings, not individual roll calls.
